answer: The ivory tower of pure computation alone cannot fend off attackers who threaten to flood the system with forged identities. Instead, the network builds a physical jetty of proof-of-capital where each proposed agent must lock value—such as compute cycles, data, or tokens—to participate. This economic dockyard makes sybil attacks prohibitively expensive, as each fake identity demands a real stake, transforming abstract digital forgeries into costly physical commitments.
